title: Adentris vs CorroHealth: RCM Services vs BH Compliance Software Compared
summary: Adentris vs CorroHealth for behavioral health and SUD: outsourced revenue-cycle services versus focused behavioral-health documentation compliance software with ASAM, 42 CFR Part 2, and denials.
body_markdown:
**The short version:** Adentris and CorroHealth both protect revenue, but through different models. CorroHealth is a clinically-led revenue-cycle company offering coding, CDI, auditing, and denials through services combined with proprietary AI, mainly for hospitals and health systems. Adentris is focused revenue integrity and documentation compliance software purpose-built for behavioral health and SUD, with rules like ASAM level of care and 42 CFR Part 2 and an appeals and denials module, running on any EHR. If you want an outsourced revenue-cycle partner, CorroHealth is built for that. If you want behavioral-health-specific software you run in-house, that is where Adentris fits.


Both protect revenue, but through different models, so the comparison comes down to services versus focused software and specialty depth. Here is an honest comparison.


## What Adentris does


Adentris is an AI platform for revenue integrity and documentation compliance built specifically for behavioral health and SUD programs. It works on top of the EHR you already run, connecting through an API or HL7 where one exists (for example Alleva, Pimsy, Kipu, Epic, or Athenahealth) and through a secure web agent where it does not, so there is no migration. It reviews notes in real time and flags the elements that get behavioral health claims denied before the claim is submitted: medical necessity, ASAM level-of-care justification, treatment plan updates, group therapy attendance, service units, signature timing, and 42 CFR Part 2 consent. When something is missing, it drafts the correction for the clinician to accept, and it pairs documentation review with an appeals and denials module. Adentris is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, with 42 CFR Part 2 controls and BAAs in place.


## What CorroHealth does


CorroHealth is a clinically-led revenue-cycle management company that combines services with proprietary technology across coding, clinical documentation integrity, auditing, and denials, including automation and clinician-led appeals, largely for hospitals and health systems. For organizations that want an outsourced, technology-enabled revenue-cycle partner, CorroHealth is a strong, established option.

## Which should you choose?


Both protect revenue, so the real question is model and specialty depth. CorroHealth is a services-plus-technology partner that takes on broad revenue-cycle work for hospitals. Adentris is focused software that a behavioral health or SUD program runs on top of its own EHR, built around the denials specific to the field: ASAM level of care, medical necessity, group therapy attendance, service units, and 42 CFR Part 2 consent. Adentris reviews the note in real time before submission, drafts the correction, and pairs review with an appeals and denials module, running on any EHR through a secure web agent. For a behavioral health or SUD program that wants purpose-built software, that focus is the practical difference.


- **Choose CorroHealth if** you want an outsourced, technology-enabled revenue-cycle partner to take on broad coding, CDI, auditing, and denials.
- **Choose Adentris if** you run a behavioral health or SUD program and want focused, in-house software that reviews documentation against the specialty rules that drive denials, with drafted fixes and appeals, on any EHR.


## Adentris as a CorroHealth alternative for behavioral health and SUD


If you are evaluating CorroHealth for a behavioral health or SUD program, the question is model and specialty fit. A broad outsourced revenue-cycle partner is valuable at health-system scale, but behavioral health claims are denied for field-specific reasons: an unjustified ASAM level of care, a missing medical necessity statement, group therapy attendance and service units that do not line up, or a 42 CFR Part 2 consent that was not captured. Adentris is focused software built around those rules, reviews the note before submission, drafts the fix, pairs it with an appeals and denials workflow, and runs on any EHR through an API, HL7, or a secure web agent, which makes it the purpose-built choice for behavioral health and SUD.


## How Adentris helps


For behavioral health and SUD organizations, the biggest revenue leak is documentation, and it is specific: medical necessity that was never shown, missing ASAM justification, a Part 2 consent that was not captured. Adentris reviews every chart in real time inside your existing EHR and flags exactly those gaps before the claim is filed, then drafts the fix, and it pairs that with an appeals and denials module so compliance and revenue integrity live in one place. In practice that means fewer denied claims, less audit exposure, and far less time spent reworking documentation after a payer pushes back. Adentris is HIPAA compliant and SOC 2 certified, with 42 CFR Part 2 controls and BAAs in place. For an outsourced, broad revenue-cycle partner, CorroHealth is a strong fit. For a behavioral health or SUD program that wants focused in-house software, Adentris brings the specialty depth, ASAM, medical necessity, and 42 CFR Part 2, drafts the fix before submission, and pairs it with appeals, on any EHR.

## Frequently asked questions


**What is the difference between Adentris and CorroHealth?**


CorroHealth is a clinically-led revenue-cycle company offering coding, CDI, auditing, and denials through services plus proprietary AI, mainly for hospitals. Adentris is focused revenue integrity and documentation compliance software purpose-built for behavioral health and SUD, with ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 rules and an appeals module, running on any EHR. The main difference is model and specialty depth: outsourced RCM services versus behavioral-health-specific software.


**Can Adentris and CorroHealth be used together?**


Yes. They solve different halves of the problem, so a program can use CorroHealth to run outsourced revenue-cycle work and Adentris to verify the documentation supports the claim and to handle appeals. Adentris reviews the note however it was written, so it fits alongside CorroHealth.


**Is Adentris a good alternative to CorroHealth?**


For programs whose problem is denials and audit exposure rather than outsourced revenue-cycle services, yes. Adentris focuses on catching and correcting the behavioral health and SUD gaps that drive denials before submission, with ASAM and 42 CFR Part 2 built in and an appeals and denials module, and it runs on any EHR without a migration.


**Which is better for a substance use disorder program?**


For SUD, the claims that get denied usually turn on ASAM level of care, medical necessity, and 42 CFR Part 2, which Adentris is built around with real-time, pre-submission review and drafted corrections. CorroHealth is strong for clinically-led revenue-cycle services across coding, CDI, and denials. Programs that want SUD-specific compliance depth and denials support often lean Adentris.
